title: Stabilization flow: install/upgrade troubleshooting + Terraform module notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working stabilization flow for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) focused on common install/runtime failures seen during fresh installs and rolling upgrades. It pairs a minimal smoke-test checklist with concise Terraform module notes and a pragmatic rollback/mitigation ladder. Use this doc as the first-stop triage flow for field incidents and as a reference for runbooks we will later formalize into the official playbook.

Scope and constraints:
- Targets: single-cluster on-prem and VPC-connected Private deployments (control plane + runtime nodes).
- Not a complete runbook; assumes SRE or SE on-call has cluster admin access and the deployment's Terraform state/backend credentials.
- Emphasis on quick stabilization to restore request-serving; deeper postmortem/root-cause to follow.

1) Quick triage (first 10 minutes)
- Goal: identify whether failures are configuration, infra, or runtime.
- Quick checks (do in parallel if possible):
  * Ping control plane endpoints from an admin jump host (curl -v): control-plane.api:8443/healthz
  * Check whether pods are running: kubectl get pods -n redwood --no-headers -o wide
  * Check node readiness: kubectl get nodes -o wide
  * Verify Terraform backend/state access (from CI or operations host): terraform -chdir=infra plan -var-file=secrets.tfvars
  * Check disk pressure and memory on hosts: ssh node 'free -m && df -h /var/lib/containerd'
  * Look for GVNIC/eni or CNI errors in system logs: journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i cni

Interpreting the quick results:
- All pods CrashLoopBackOff / Image pull errors => likely registry/auth or image tag mismatch. Check imagePullSecrets and registry reachable from nodes.
- Control plane healthy but service endpoints failing (503) => check ingress / service mappings and route table (load balancer) health.
- Terraform plan failures or locked state => infra level; do not run forced state changes unless you have a backup.
- Node NotReady with kernel/oom/disk issues => node-level remediation (reboot/containerd cleanup).

2) Smoke-test checklist (sequence, stop on failure)
- Preconditions: kubeconfig pointed at target cluster, TF state accessible.
- Commands / checks:
  1. kubectl get ns redwood || kubectl create ns redwood  # namespace existence
  2. kubectl run smoke-hello --image=alpine -n redwood --restart=Never --command -- sh -c 'echo OK' && kubectl logs -n redwood smoke-hello
  3. curl -sS --fail https://control-plane.api:8443/healthz | head -n 5
  4. kubectl rollout status deploy/redwood-runtime -n redwood --timeout=3m
  5. kubectl exec -n redwood deploy/redwood-runtime -- ls /var/lib/redwood || true  # KV cache dir check
  6. curl -sS http://<local-runtime-ip>:8080/readyz  # runtime readiness probe
  7. run a short inference (sample request): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' http://<ingress-host>/v1/generate | jq -r '.choices[0].text'

- If any step fails, capture logs and key artifacts: kubectl describe pod <pod>, kubectl logs -c runtime <pod>, journalctl -u docker -n 200 (or containerd). Attach to incident ticket.

3) Common failure patterns and rapid remedies
- TF: "Error: Error locking state" or stuck apply
  * Cause: multiple concurrent apply, misconfigured remote backend, or state file corruption.
  * Remediation: verify lock owner via backend UI (S3/Dynamo/consul). If appropriate, confirm with owner and force-unlock (terraform force-unlock <ID>) only after snapshotting state (terraform state pull > state.json). Document unlock action.
- Image pulls failing (manifest unknown / unauthorized)
  * Cause: expired registry token, incorrect image tag, private registry network restrictions.
  * Remediation: test docker pull from node, check imagePullSecrets in namespace, rotate registry creds if expired.
- Runtime process OOMs after upgrade
  * Cause: new model variant with higher memory footprint, wrong resource requests/limits, or missing GPU scheduling changes.
  * Remediation: scale replicas down, revert to previous model tag, adjust limits, or fast-rollback via helm/manifest to previous image.
- KV cache corruption / missing snapshots
  * Cause: disk full, unexpected shutdown, or incompatible storage mount after upgrade.
  * Remediation: stop runtime, restore cache directory from last snapshot (path documented in upgrade notes), start in degraded mode (skip cache) to allow traffic while full restoration is performed.
- TLS/Cert rotation causing control-plane 502/504
  * Cause: expired certs or mis-propagated secrets during rotation.
  * Remediation: check cert-manager or secret sync; re-issue certs and restart ingress components; use short-lived bypass (HTTP) only if permitted by compliance.

4) Terraform module notes (summary / gotchas)
- Module: redwood-vpc (networking)
  * State sharding: VPC module uses a dedicated state file (backend key: vpc/<env>). Do not apply cross-module changes in a single apply unless you coordinate across module owners.
  * Common pitfalls: changing subnet assignments after runtime created causes route table mismatches; if you must change subnets, drain nodes and run a rolling replacement with new AMIs/config.
- Module: redwood-ctrlplane (control plane infra)
  * Provider version pinning: we pin aws provider ~> 4.0; applying with newer provider versions may silently change resource graphs (IAM role names). Always run a plan and diff before apply.
  * IAM & RBAC drift: upgrades that change IAM assume-role ARNs can break node bootstrap; validate IAM roles are not replaced during apply.
- Module: redwood-runtime (kubernetes resources & node pools)
  * Nodepool upgrades often change GPU drivers — include a canary node pool for driver validation.
  * Terraform lifecycle rules: we set create_before_destroy for daemonset-managed volumes; changing this can orphan PVs. Check lifecycle blocks before changing storage classes.

TF upgrade/apply best practices (short list)
- Always run terraform plan and store plan output (terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan) and attach to ticket.
- Use a staging apply in a mirrored staging workspace before prod.
- If a plan replaces >5 resources or touches state keys for core infra (subnets, LB, IAM), escalate to oncall lead and schedule a maintenance window.
- Snapshot state before significant changes: terraform state pull > state-YYYYMMDD.json, upload to secure S3.

5) Minimal rollback ladder (fast -> safer)
- If a single deployment is failing after a manifest change: kubectl rollout undo deploy/<name> -n redwood
- If a model image causes OOMs: revert runtime image tag in deployment/helm values and redeploy, scale down heavier replicas first.
- If a TF change impacted networking: rollback using the previous TF plan (terraform apply "plan.tfplan") from staging or restore state snapshot and re-run apply.
- Full environment rollback: only after approval — restore VM/node snapshots or use infra automation that has known good AMI/instance templates.

6) Logs and diagnostic artifacts to collect (attach to ticket)
- kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide > pods.txt
- kubectl describe pod <failing-pod> > describe.txt
- kubectl logs -n redwood <pod> -c runtime > runtime.log
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 > kubelet.log
- terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan (attach binary) and terraform state pull > state.json
- node /var/log/messages or /var/log/syslog for kernel reboots

7) Short checklist for upgrades (preflight + postflight)
- Preflight (48h before): run workload profile collection (p95 token lengths, concurrency), verify capacity headroom >= 30%
- Preflight (30m before): run smoke-test checklist against current prod; snapshot TF state and etcd (if self-hosted).
- During upgrade: apply to control plane canary, run smoke tests, then apply runtime canary with reduced traffic.
- Postflight (immediate): run smoke-test checklist and run 10 synthetic user flows at expected concurrency for 10 minutes.
- Postflight (24h): watch quality metrics + cost deltas for regressions.

8) Notes and TODOs (local working items)
- TODO: Add automated 'smoke-runner' job that executes the smoke-test checklist from an internal Kong-proxied test harness. (Ticket: PD-9342)
- TODO: Document the KV cache snapshot/restore CLI and embed examples in the next revision of the install guide. (Assigned: Ravi)
- TODO: Add a TF pre-apply hook that warns if plan changes > 5 infra resources.

Appendix: quick command references
- kubectl logs -n redwood deploy/redwood-runtime -c runtime --tail=200 > /tmp/runtime-tail.log
- ssh ops@node-01 'sudo systemctl restart containerd && sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager'
- terraform -chdir=infra init && terraform -chdir=infra plan -out=plan.tfplan -var-file=secrets.tfvars

If you used this doc for an active incident, add a summary to the incident ticket with which step resolved the issue and upload collected artifacts. This file is a draft — please add edge cases you encounter and ping authors to promote to final playbook when stable.
